LESSON: CULTURE AND SOCIAL ORGANISATION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Culture and Social Organisation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Culture and Social Organisation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How would we preserve positive aspects of African traditional culture?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe age-groups and age- sets in African traditional society
2. explain the functions of a clan in traditional African society
3. identify aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CULTURE AND SOCIAL ORGANISATION
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Culture and Social Organisation helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: CULTURE AND SOCIAL ORGANISATION
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Describe age-groups and age- sets in African traditional society

What this means
In this part you learn to describe age-groups and age- sets in African traditional society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe age-groups and age- sets in African traditional society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Culture and Social Organisation” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe age-groups and age- sets in African traditional society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the functions of a clan in traditional African society

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the functions of a clan in traditional African society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the functions of a clan in traditional African society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Culture and Social Organisation.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the functions of a clan in traditional African society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Identify aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved

What this means
In this part you learn to identify aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Culture and Social Organisation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Culture and Social Organisation” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: describe age-groups and age- sets in African traditional society)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Culture and Social Organisation. (skill: explain the functions of a clan in traditional African society)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: identify aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Culture and Social Organisation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe age-groups and age- sets in African traditional society.
3. Practise this skill: explain the functions of a clan in traditional African society.
4. Practise this skill: identify aspects of African traditional culture that ought to be preserved.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Culture and Social Organisation from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Culture and Social Organisation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Culture and Social Organisation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How would we preserve positive aspects of African traditional culture?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Culture and Social Organisation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe age-groups and age- sets in African traditional society.
5. Be able to: explain the functions of a clan in traditional African society.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
